items.body: TORONTO -- All is quiet between the Minnesota Wild and Quinn Hughes , and the team could keep the defenseman past the NHL Trade Deadline on March 1 if he doesn’t sign a new deal, general manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday. Hughes, whom the Wild acquired from the Vancouver Canucks in a trade Dec. 12, 2025, is in the final season of a six-year, $47.1 million contract ($7.85 million average annual value) he signed with Vancouver on Oct. 3, 2021. The 27-year-old has been eligible to sign a new contract with the Wild since July 1. If he doesn’t sign before June 30, he will become an unrestricted free agent the next day. On Oct. 24, Hughes said he “wouldn’t be surprised if something happens soon.” But Tuesday, Guerin said the situation is “status quo.” “Because, honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” Would Guerin be willing to keep Hughes past the trade deadline? Hughes won the Norris Trophy as the NHL’s best defenseman in 2024. Since the trade, Hughes has 80 points (11 goals, 69 assists) in 68 games, second on the Wild and second among NHL defensemen. In that span, forward Kirill Kaprizov leads Minnesota with 87 points (44 goals, 43 assists) in 67 games, and Evan Bouchard of the Edmonton Oilers is first among NHL defensemen with 98 points (26 goals, 72 assists) in 70 games. The Wild (13-3-4), who extended their point streak to nine games (7-0-2) with a 2-1 overtime win at the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday, lead the Central Division. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin said. “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.”

items.title: Price tribute should leave lasting impression on young Canadiens
items.summary: The scene as Montreal paid tribute to Carey Price before Tuesday’s game will stay with the Canadiens and goaltender Jacob Fowler forever.
items.body: MONTREAL — Shortly before taking the ice to one of the most rousing ovations in Bell Centre history, Carey Price was asked for his favourite memory in the building he called home for 15 years. “Probably that night with Patrick (Roy’s jersey) retirement,” Price said. “That was really special, and I have a picture of that in my memorabilia room. It’s pretty special to be part of something like this.” That was one special evening. Nov. 22, 2008, the night 33 was immortalized. No one remembers that it ended with Price fittingly making 33 saves and not so fittingly losing 3-2 in the shootout to the Boston Bruins. Least of all him, apparently. For Price could’ve chosen any of the 202 wins he registered in a Montreal Canadiens home uniform as his most cherished memory. He could’ve referenced one of the 22 wins he recorded when it mattered most in front of these fans—in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. But the night Price watched his hero have his number retired was the one that stayed with the goaltender more than any other because it reinforced how special it is to be a Canadien and reconnected him with his childhood dream. It is the shared dream of every hockey-loving child, but certainly the ones with true NHL aspirations. They don’t close their eyes and picture playing in the three-quarter full buildings of tax-free states. They don’t think about the comfort anonymity provides in a sunbelt market. No, the dream is playing out a Hall of Fame career in a mecca like Montreal, of leaving it all on the ice for fans who chant your name at full throat until they go hoarse. The fantasy is coming back for one more dose of that, like Roy did almost exactly 18 years to the day Price did. "Yeah, I mean, you have to be a dominant team at home and then you have to be a very good road team," Avalanche forward Gabriel Landeskog said. "If you want to be that dominant team that you want to be and go where you want to go that is most definitely the objective." The Avalanche got off to a strong start to their four-game road stretch with a 6-3 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena on Tuesday. But what happens next in Ottawa on Thursday, then in Montreal on Saturday and finally in Utah a week from Wednesday will either allow them to feel settled into the season or continue what has been a topsy-turvy first quarter for the Stanley Cup contender. You never want to place too much emphasis on a stretch of four games in an 84-game season, and the Avalanche (11-6-2) aren't doing that, but they feel the importance of these four games, especially considering what road life has been like for them so far this season. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images The Ottawa Senators suffered a tough 3-2 overtime loss to the Washington Capitals on Tuesday, but the well-being of forward Nick Cousins is their biggest concern coming out of the game. Late in the third period, Cousins was picking up the puck deep in his own zone and got absolutely hammered by a crushing body check from Capitals defenseman Jakob Chychrun. The hit sent Cousins careening into the glass, and he lay motionless on the ice for some time before eventually getting helped to the Senators’ dressing room. Since the hit targeted Cousins’ chest and Chychrun did not leave his feet, there was no penalty assessed on the play. After the game, Senators head coach Travis Green gave a less than promising update on Cousins’ status. Cousins, 33, has two goals and an assist for three points in 19 games this played this season. Last season, he put up nine goals and 14 assists for 23 points in 81 games before contributing no goals and an assist in Ottawa’s first-round playoff loss to the Carolina Hurricanes in four games. Selected by the Philadelphia Flyers in the third round of the 2011 NHL Entry Draft, the Belleville, Ontario native has played for six different teams over 13 NHL seasons. Best known as an agitator and bottom-six forechecker, Cousins has never put up more than 27 points in a season, a number he reached in the 2018-19 season with the Arizona Coyotes, and then again in the 2022-23 season with the Florida Panthers . He won a Stanley Cup with the Panthers in the 2023-24 season. Given the impact of Chychrun’s hit, the concern is that Cousins suffered a concussion. I think at this point, given what I have going on …” “It’s a convenient time to kind of see everybody,” he continued. “But again, for me, I’m taking it day by day as it goes here and enjoying the whole process.” Horcoff said it was “status quo” with center Dylan Larkin and defenseman Simon Edvinsson . Larkin, 30, asked for a trade after last season while using the no-trade clause in his contract to limit Detroit’s options. He left the team Oct. 29 and is suspended without pay . The six-time 30-goal scorer is in the fourth year of an eight-year, $69.9 million contract he signed with Detroit ($8.7 million average annual value) on March 1, 2023. Horcoff declined to comment on whether Larkin has altered the list of teams to which he would agree to be traded. “Ideally, we get something that works for both sides, right?” Horcoff said. “But it has to be something that helps this team.” Edvinsson, 23, is an unsigned restricted free agent currently working out in Nashville. He reportedly wants to be traded. Horcoff has said he has no interest in trading Edvinsson, who must sign by Dec. 1 to be eligible to play this season. “I’d still like to sign Simon, but I think when it’s someone like that and the situation that we’re in, you can’t help but take calls,” Horcoff said. “It’s my job to do what’s in the best interest of the Detroit Red Wings. items.body: Terrence Lee-Imagn Images Terrence Lee-Imagn Images 'Expected Win Probability 100%': Social Media Reacts To Jets' Win In Hellebuyck's Return To Winnipeg Eric Cruikshank Partner Nov 11, 2026 3:46 AM Published Nov 11, 2026 3:46 AM With months of frustration building in anticipation of Connor Hellebuyck's return, Winnipeg Jets fans delivered. Hellebuyck made his highly anticipated trip back to Canada Life Centre on Tuesday for the first time since being traded to the New Jersey Devils . While he didn't start between the pipes in this contest, that didn't stop Jets fans from having their voices heard. More Videos Before the puck even dropped, the 33-year-old was welcomed with a smattering of boos and creative signage from the Winnipeg crowd as he took some warmup laps and faced a handful of shots. Similarly to Brady Tkachuk's return to Ottawa and Quinn Hughes' return to Vancouver, Hellebuyck - despite not being visible to fans throughout the game - received echoes of creative cheers In poetic fashion, it would be Dawson Mercer, one of the main pieces in the Devils' package they sent to acquire Hellebuyck, opened the scoring and finished with two goals. The 24-year-old was named the first star of the game for his efforts, and was praised by viewers on social media for his efforts. "You don't trade a player like Dawson Mercer." @MikeBartner added. "Dawson Mercer may have become a Winnipeg Jets legend." @ACoronaNJD proclaimed. In addition to Mercer, former Devils goaltender Nico Daws - who was also part of the Hellebuyck trade - got the nod for the Jets in this game and made 19 saves for his first victory with the franchise. "Good for Nico Daws. That's a tough atmosphere to stay composed in and he delivered." @tj_maughan wrote. "Dawson Mercer & Nico Daws revenge game!" @Sheeps

With the primary assist on Cole Hutson ‘s overtime game-winning goal against the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night, Ovechkin has now tied Nicklas Backstrom for the most assists in Capitals franchise history. The helper was the 762nd of Ovechkin’s legendary career and his fourth this season. Backstrom finished his Capitals career with 762 assists in 1,105 games. Hutson did the heavy lifting on the goal, as Ovechkin kicked him the puck a full eight seconds before the rookie defender beat Senators goaltender Samuel Ersson to the far side of the net. The marker was Hutson’s second point of the game after he recorded the primary assist on Pierre-Luc Dubois ‘ third-period goal to tie the game. Ovechkin’s 762nd assist comes three years and 16 days after Backstrom recorded the final assist of his career against the New Jersey Devils on October 25, 2023. Backstrom’s apple was the second on a goal scored by Connor McMichael , which ended up being the game-winning marker in a 6-4 win over the Devils. The high-scoring Swedish centerman would play just two more games with the Capitals before stepping away from the team due to recurring issues with his surgically repaired hip. He sat out the rest of the 2023-24 season and the entirety of the 2024-25 season before returning to hockey with his hometown team, Brynäs IF, in the SHL for the 2025-26 campaign. items.body: Former Devils forward Dawson Mercer and Kyle Connor each scored twice to lead the Winnipeg Jets to an emotional 4-2 victory over New Jersey on Tuesday. The victory extended Winnipeg's win streak to four games, and halted New Jersey’s at five games. Former Devils netminder Nico Daws made 19 saves for Winnipeg (8-8-3) before a capacity crowd of 15,321 fans at Canada Life Centre. After Mercer gave the Jets a 3-2 lead on the power play at 11:58 of the third period, Connor sealed the outcome with an unassisted empty-net goal. The Devils, who trailed 2-0 after the first period, tied the game in the second period with a pair of goals 44 seconds apart. Bratt scored at 1:14 on a perfect setup from Arseny Gritsyuk from behind the net. Jack Hughes also assisted to extend his point streak to six games. Glass then tied the game at 1:58 when he deflected Jonathan Kovacevic’s shot past Daws. Declan Chisholm also assisted. Connor scored during a two-man advantage at 15:06 of the first period when he deflected Cole Perfetti’s pass past Allen. Mark Scheifele also assisted, moving him into a second-place tie with Dale Hawerchuk in all-time assists in franchise history with 550. Mercer opened the scoring at 7:54 when his snap shot from the faceoff circle beat Allen. items.summary: Cole Hutson’s goal 74 seconds into overtime, set up by Alex Ovechkin, lifted the Washington Capitals to a 3-2 win over the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday.
items.body: The Ottawa Senators had one of their better performances of the season on Tuesday but still ended up in the loss column. The Senators (11-6-2) outworked, outmuscled and outshot the Washington Capitals but couldn’t outscore the visitors, falling 3-2 in overtime. The bright side was the fact they still managed to earn a point. The Senators have been without starting goaltender Linus Ullmark for almost three weeks but have managed to hold their own and play some impressive hockey. The Senators have gone 4-3-2 without Ullmark, thanks in large part to 27-year-old Samuel Ersson of Sweden, who seems to be finding his game, and the team remaining committed to smart decisions with and without the puck. Tuesday was a perfect example. Washington scored on its first shot and outshot Ottawa 11-5 in the opening 20 minutes. From the start of the second, the Senators dominated and outshot the Capitals 17-2 — holding the American squad without a shot for more than 21 minutes. “I thought we played awesome tonight,” said Senators head coach Travis Green. “It was one of our better games of the year.” Not one to be lavish in his praise, Green said he liked everything about his team’s game. “Thought we checked well,” he said. “We created a lot. Put a lot of pressure on the back end.” Early in the season the Senators often had to rely on Tim Stutzle and Drake Batherson to carry the offensive load, but in their last three games Ottawa has been getting depth scoring from the likes of Michael Amadio, Fabian Zetterlund, Ridly Greig and Nick Cousins. items.body: Devils goalie reiterates love for Winnipeg, but some things ‘crossed the line’ WINNIPEG -- Connor Hellebuyck said his family’s safety and uncertainly about his career played a part in requesting a trade from the Winnipeg Jets at the end of last season. But the New Jersey Devils goalie would not point to one thing that made him decide to ask out. “There’s no one singular moment that wasn’t important in all of this decision-making and this is over a span of time,” Hellebuyck said in his return to Canada Life Centre on Tuesday. “I will say with all the uncertainty I was experiencing, there was some moments and some things that happened to my family that for me crossed the line. And as a husband and a father, I felt made that decision very certain, that I needed to be a good husband and a good father and do what’s best for my family and my career.” Hellebuyck, who was traded by the Jets to the Devils on Oct. 23, was addressing the Winnipeg media for the first time since his exit interview April 17, after the Jets failed to qualify for the Stanley Cup Playoffs. items.title: Senators’ Cousins exits after big hit from Capitals’ Chychrun
items.body: The Ottawa Senators went down a forward late in Tuesday's game against the Washington Capitals . Nick Cousins was forced to exit the game after he was on the receiving end of a massive hit from Capitals defenceman Jakob Chychrun with three minutes remaining in the third period. As Cousins was looking to clear the puck out of the defensive end, Chychrun caught the Senators forward with his head down and sent him flying into the boards. Cousins stayed face down on the ice before eventually getting to his feet and making his way off the ice with assistance from teammates. He would not return for the remainder of the game. "He's not doing great," head coach Travis Green said after the game . The officials reviewed the hit for a five-minute major, but determined that there was no penalty on the hit.

items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Heinen, Hanifin, Marchment, Panthers By Bradley Keith | at November 10, 2026 7:54 pm According to Aaron Portzline of The Athletic , Columbus forward Danton Heinen did not “immediately” report to AHL Cleveland last week after he cleared waivers . The veteran is reportedly weighing his options while the Blue Jackets organization is giving him the time needed to figure out next steps in his career. Coming up on a decade since his 47-point debut campaign in Boston, the 31-year-old has become more of a rotational depth forward at this point in his career and no longer the strong third line two-way winger he once was. Still, it’s not hard to see why Heinen would want to assess where his career goes next. The 2014 fourth-round pick (Boston) has skated in just 17 AHL games since the 2016-17 season as a prospect. A 12-game stint with the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins last season proved he still had more in the tank, dominating with 17 points in 12 games. Heinen accepted a two-way deal to stick around in Ohio for the season, making the team but coming away scoreless in his 10 games, averaging 10:10 a night, the lowest usage of his 11-year career. Currently 26th in the AHL the Monsters already have a roster full of veterans including Steven Lorentz , who has lit it up with seven goals in nine games, as well as Carson Soucy who just joined the club. Whatever happens ahead, Columbus respectfully is making sure they do right of the British Columbia native who has skated in 622 NHL games in his career.

items.body: TORONTO — Count Toronto Maple Leafs GM John Chayka among those not surprised to hear defenceman Chris Tanev 's reaction to the team’s load management plan that will ration his use over the course of the season. He’s made a career out of being that player and takes a lot of pride in being available to play every night. “From our side, we do have an obligation to the players and to the organization to do the right thing and consider a player’s long-term health. And to do the right thing for the organization for the short-term and long-term. We respect that Chris wants to play.” Tanev, 36, missed all but 11 games last season after sustaining a serious concussion. This season, he suffered an injury on Oct. 10 against the Colorado Avalanche and then missed nine games. Coach Jim Hiller said that while he wished he could have Tanev in the lineup each night, “there’s a plan in place to protect the player and the team.” Chayka said: “We’re taking in a lot of information and making decisions. items.title: Hellebuyck sends mixed message to Jets fans seeking closure
items.summary: In Connor Hellebuyck’s careful attempt to prevent this from becoming a sticky situation, he has completely muddied the waters regarding why he abandoned the only NHL home he has ever known.
items.body: WINNIPEG — In his much-anticipated return to Winnipeg on Tuesday, Connor Hellebuyck desperately tried to keep his story straight. But in his careful attempt to prevent his departure from Winnipeg from becoming a sticky situation, the former franchise goaltender has completely muddied the waters regarding why he abandoned the only NHL home he has ever known. Sitting in front of dozens of reporters at Canada Life Centre, Hellebuyck looked and acted like a man wanting to have his cake and eat it, too. Rather than speak clearly and concisely about the treatment he received from disappointed Canadians and a clear desire to move his family south of the border, Hellebuyck opted to dance around the subject. Only adding insult to injury, Hellebuyck won't even face the music Tuesday against his former team. Despite his insistence that he felt a "duty" to play, New Jersey Devils general manager Sunny Mehta stepped in with a dizzying analytics-led excuse. Citing a "reduction in our expected win probability," Mehta is sitting his all-star goalie. The irony of Hellebuyck demanding out of Winnipeg, where he had full control of his playing time, to join an organization that now dictates his ice time through analytics is too difficult to ignore. But to understand just how brazen it was for Hellebuyck to sit at a table inside Canada Life Centre and ask fans to separate his exit from his legacy, you have to look at how that exit played out. "The day I said I was a Jet for life, I meant it," Hellebuyck said. "But I also didn't foresee the future that was going to happen." items.title: NHL to explore replay assist technology for officials
items.summary: NHL commissioner Gary Bettman was quick to remind that wholesale changes won’t be coming to the way the game is officiated, but he mentioned how tech advancements might streamline everything from information to the flow of the game.
items.body: TORONTO — Remember a few weeks ago when Buffalo’s Owen Power was incensed that he was wrongly whistled for a high-sticking penalty? It was friendly fire. Power didn’t high-stick Matvei Michkov, who was done dirty by his own teammate, Trevor Zegras. All 18,000 fans in KeyBank Arena in Buffalo saw it on replay. The NHL’s Situation Room saw it in near real time. But once the call is made on the ice, according to current rules, there’s no chance to review it and it cannot be rescinded. “The only four people that don’t get to see it are the four guys in striped shirts,” NHL senior executive vice president of hockey operations Colin Campbell said. “There’s times we would like to get involved.” To that end, Campbell said the NHL will explore in the coming months how things like rapid replay assist technology can aid on-ice officials. Think something that wouldn’t involve a long huddle or review, but how quickly, as in the NFL, the spot of the ball is corrected, or how fast it is relayed to the officiating team that a runner stepped out of bounds. “The game’s not perfect,” Campbell said. “How can we help them out? “You look at football, what they’ve done with the quarterback’s helmet. You look at baseball, with the pitcher and catcher (pitchcom device). All sports are expanding communication.” The discussion was brought to the NHL’s 32 general managers in their meeting on Tuesday and Campbell said the “appetite was good.” Rule changes cannot be enacted mid-season but can be voted on in Florida in March for the Competition Committee to implement for 2027-28. items.body: According to a report from NHL insider Kevin Weekes of ESPN, Michkov would prefer to have a fresh start with another team, with Weekes referring to him as a “very, very much in-demand potential trade target.” Michkov is in his third NHL season after the Flyers selected him with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2023 NHL Draft. The Flyers performed well last season en route to an appearance in the second round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs, but the team has struggled mightily out of the gate this year. Philadelphia owns a 5-10-5 record, the worst in the Eastern Conference by points percentage. Michkov has earned more ice time from Tocchet this season, up to 15:54 per game, and he leads the Flyers with 10 goals. items.title: NHL, NHLPA to discuss possibility of ‘smoothing’ salary cap over next two seasons
items.summary: The NHL’s salary cap will be $113.5 million next season, and is projected to be $127.5 million in the 2028-29 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The NHL’s salary cap has increased substantially over the last couple of seasons, leading to some monstrous contracts getting handed out this past offseason. It’s expected to continue to skyrocket in the years to come. According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , however, the league is looking at the possibility of “smoothing” the salary cap’s growth over the next two seasons. At Tuesday’s GM meetings, it was decided that the NHL and NHLPA will meet in the new year to discuss ways of making the salary cap’s increases over the next couple seasons less dramatic year over year, with the hopes of creating a more stable salary environment across the league. The NHL’s salary cap this season is $104 million, which increased from $95.5 million last season and $88 million the season prior. It will grow to $113.5 million next season, and is currently projected to be $127.5 million in the 2028-29 season. According to Friedman, one strategy the league could pursue is raising next season’s cap from $113.5 million by a certain amount, and then lowering the 2028-29 cap by the same amount, thereby shrinking the cap spike between the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons. For example, if next year’s cap is raised from $113.5 to $115.5 million, representing a $2 million bump, then the cap for the 2028-29 season would be decreased by $2 million, going from a projected $127.5 million to a projected $125.5 million. This would keep the difference between the 2027-28 and 2028-29 salary caps to $10 million. items.summary: There has been no joy for the Canucks so far. And on several nights, some essential pride has been missing too, as Vancouver crashed to its worst opening quarter in franchise history.
items.body: VANCOUVER — Losing hockey games is not the same thing as playing losing hockey. Coach Manny Malhotra warned everyone about this ahead of the first full season of the Vancouver Canucks ’ rebuild. “There’s a very big difference between losing games, which is inevitable. . . and playing losing hockey,” Malhotra told reporters on the eve of training camp in September. “The measure of our group will be on playing the right way, doing the things that we’re talking about, having details to your game, which is going to give us an opportunity to win. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images The Minnesota Wild are welcoming their captain back into the fold. On Tuesday, the Wild announced that they have activated defenseman Jared Spurgeon off of injured reserve. In a corresponding move, the Wild have assigned forward Tyler Pitlick to their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Iowa Wild. Spurgeon, 36, has missed Minnesota’s last five games , and was also out for a four-game stretch with an upper-body injury earlier this season. In 10 games played so far, the Edmonton native has a goal and four assists for five points while averaging about 20 and a half minutes of ice time. Last season, Spurgeon notched six goals and 16 assists for 22 points in 79 games while averaging about 19 and a half minutes of ice time. He then put up no goals and an assist while averaging a tick over 21 minutes in 11 playoff games. Selected by the New York Islanders in the sixth round of the 2008 NHL Entry Draft, Spurgeon did not sign his entry-level deal with New York and instead signed with Minnesota after his five-year junior career with the Spokane Chiefs of the Western Hockey League (WHL). Spurgeon is now in his 17th NHL season, all with the Wild. He ranks second in games played on Minnesota’s all-time list with 1,022, just six games back of Mikko Koivu. He also ranks third on the Wild’s all-time scoring list with 443 points. He is in the final season of a seven-year, $53.03 million contract . Pitlick, 35, has gone scoreless in 12 games played for Minnesota this season. The Minneapolis, Minnesota native has played for nine different teams over parts of 12 seasons in the NHL. items.title: NHL, NHLPA to discuss salary-cap options in new year
items.body: Frank Seravalli will have a full recap of today’s GM meetings later today on sportsnet.ca, but a quickie blog on one additional item from Tuesday's meetup. The NHL and NHLPA will meet in the new year to discuss the possibility of “smoothing” the salary cap over the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons. Under the current three-year agreement — which concludes at the end of next season — the salary cap for 2027-28 will be $113.5 million. At September’s Board of Governors meeting in New York City, the league provided a preliminary estimate of $127.5 million for 2028-29. What the league and players’ association could agree to is raising next season’s ceiling and lowering the 2028-29 number by the same amount. For example, if they decided to raise 2027-28 by $2 million to $115.5 million, they would drop the following year to $125.5 million. Again, there is nothing concrete at this time, just a willingness to discuss the issue over the next few months. The NBA went through something similar after a major television contract jumped its cap from $70 million in 2015-16 to $94 million in 2016-17. After it was decided that summer created too much carnage, the latest CBA prevents any jump being larger than 10 per cent. We’ll see what the NHL and NHLPA come up with, if both agree on a change.

The money goes directly to theNHL Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. This isn’t the first time Marchment has faced supplemental discipline in his NHL career. items.body: Connor Hellebuyck is giving a bit of insight in his decision to request a trade from the Winnipeg Jets . Returning to Winnipeg for the first time since being traded on Oct. 23, the New Jersey Devils goaltender said incidents with his family played a significant role in his decision. "There's no one singular moment that wasn't important in all of this decision making, and this is over a span of time," Hellebuyck told reporters in Winnipeg on Tuesday. "I will say, with all the uncertainty, there was, you know, some moments and some things that happened to my family that, for me, crossed the line. As a husband and a father, I felt (the incidents) made that decision very certain." Though Hellebuyck didn't specify what happened to his family, he said "it was more than online death threats." Hellebuyck was dealt from the Jets to conclude a long saga that saw the goalie suspended by his team after failing to report for training camp. The 33-year-old has three Vezina Trophies and a Hart Trophy as league MVP under his belt, all won as a member of the Jets. He backstopped the United States to Olympic gold — their first in four decades — at the 2026 Winter Olympics. items.title: Report: NHL GMs ‘warm’ to idea of video-assisted review for officials
items.summary: Plays in question would help refs get the call right on penalties they might’ve missed or mistakenly called.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Christopher Trim-Imagn Images If there hasn’t been enough video review in the game today, just wait. According to insider Frank Seravalli, NHL executive vice president and director of hockey operations Colin Campbell stated that, during a meeting among the league’s general managers on Tuesday, a discussion of video-assisted review took place. The idea is that there will be direct communication to on-ice officials to amend penalties, most notably friendly-fire high-sticking. Per Seravalli, Campbell said reception from the GMs was “warm.” There is a potential vote coming up in March, with any rule changes being implemented for the 2027-28 season. Any potential rule change would also have to be approved by the NHL Players’ Association. According to responses on social media, fans seem to be in favor of the idea of righting any wrongs by referees. The one concern would be what the video review process would be like and, more or less, how long it would take. These days, if there is a call that officials feel like they messed up on, the second ref would come over to discuss the play before making a decision to reverse the call. If there were VAR put in place for penalties, many around the game hope that it can be a quick fix, rather than a long, drawn-out review that we sometimes see for potential offsides or goalie interference penalties. There certainly would be positives in helping out the refs, who can sometimes miss infractions in real time, especially with how fast the game is played these days.

items.summary: Jake Middleton wears his family history on his left arm, quite literally. The Flames defenceman’s grandfather served in the Second World War, and Middleton shares his love with a deeply meaningful tattoo sleeve.
items.body: CALGARY — The poppy fell from his father's chest and into the grave. Jake Middleton was seven years old, standing among family and friends near the military base in Wainwright, Alta., watching as they lowered his grandfather, Robert Bruce, into the ground. Somewhere in the emotion of that moment, it came loose and tumbled onto the coffin below. One by one, those gathered for “Papa's” funeral removed their own poppies, stepped forward and tossed them into the grave, sending their final tribute down with the man they had come to say goodbye to. And every Nov. 11, when the trumpets begin to sound, that little boy comes rushing back. "You know, I always get a frog in my throat when those start playing on Remembrance Day," said the Calgary Flames defenceman. It's a memory that has never really left him. Neither has the man who inspired it. Middleton wears his family history on his left arm, quite literally. His extensive tattoo sleeve is a deeply personal tribute to his grandfather, a Second World War dispatch rider who served in North Africa, France, Germany and England. It's a remarkable piece of work, and Middleton has never been particularly shy about showing it off. Those familiar with his entertaining media availabilities know they’re often delivered shirtless. items.body: A player with a very impressive junior-hockey resume is on the verge of getting his first NHL shot. Sam O'Reilly has been recalled by the Tampa Bay Lightning , the club announced Tuesday. O'Reilly was MVP of the OHL regular season and playoffs as well as the Memorial Cup last season after leading the Kitchener Rangers to the CHL and OHL titles. He was acquired by the Rangers in a mid-season deal with the London Knights, with whom he also won a Memorial Cup and two OHL championships. O'Reilly, 20, also had eight points in seven games for bronze medal-winning Canada at last year's world junior championship. The Toronto native has two goals and four assists in 12 games with AHL Syracuse. The Lightning acquired O'Reilly in a deal with the Edmonton Oilers for Isaac Howard in July 2025. items.title: Wild could keep unsigned Quinn Hughes past trade deadline, GM says
items.body: The Minnesota Wild are going all-in on their Stanley Cup aspirations this season, even if it means losing their star defenceman to free agency. General manager Bill Guerin said Tuesday that the team might opt to keep Quinn Hughes past the trade deadline even if he does not re-sign with the Wild, running the risk of losing the one-time Norris Trophy winner for nothing. “Honestly, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes, so I mean, I want to keep him as long as I possibly can,” Guerin told reporters in Toronto, per NHL.com . “Whether it’s three months, three years, seven years, whatever, we’re a better team with Quinn Hughes.” When asked if that would extend to keeping an unsigned Hughes past the trade deadline, Guerin said yes. Hughes, in the final year of a six-year, $47.1-million contract, became eligible to re-sign with the Wild on July 1. On that front, Guerin said progress towards a deal remains "status quo." "Honestly, I just want him to focus on hockey,” Guerin said. “Like I said, he knows what’s going on in his head. He understands everything.” The Wild acquired Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks in December 2025 in exchange for Zeev Buium, Liam Ohgren, Marco Rossi and a 2026 first-round pick.

Most of the attention Tuesday night will be on former Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, who demanded a trade out of Winnipeg in the offseason and forced a move him to New Jersey a few weeks ago. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images It’s official: a former NHL sniper is heading overseas. On Tuesday, the Kontinental Hockey League announced that former NHL winger Evander Kane has signed a one-year contract with HC Sibir Novosibirsk. Kane signs with Sibir, even though multiple reports stated that he was receiving offers from teams on this side of the Atlantic. His agent, Dan Milstein, stated that Kane would be heading to the KHL during last week’s episode of DFO Rundown . The 35-year-old moves to Russia after spending the 2025-26 season with the Vancouver Canucks . On a team that finished with the worst record in the NHL, Kane managed to score 13 goals and 18 assists for 31 points, finishing sixth on the team in scoring, while appearing in 71 games. It came after a rather successful four seasons with the Edmonton Oilers , where Kane’s physical play and scoring touch helped his team reach the Western Conference Finals three times, advancing to the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and 2025. In 1,001 regular-season games, which included stops with the Buffalo Sabres , San Jose Sharks and Winnipeg Jets (formerly the Atlanta Thrashers), Kane potted 339 goals and 309 assists for 648 pints, with another 55 points in 97 postseason contests. This won’t be the first time Kane has played in Russia. During the lockout that canceled half of the 2012-13 season, he signed with Dynamo Minsk, scoring two points in 12 games. Sibir is 8-1-4-13 so far this season, sitting with the worst record in the KHL’s Eastern Conference and 20th in the league’s overall standings. While it’s not clear when Kane will make his debut, Novosibirsk is in action on Sunday, taking on Dynamo Moscow.

According to the KHL , Evander Kane has signed a one-year contract with Sibir Novosibirsk in the KHL. Earlier in November, in speaking to David Pagnotta on DFO Insider , Dan Milstein of Gold Star Hockey confirmed that Evander Kane would sign with a KHL organization and that a formal announcement should be expected in the next few days; the team has officially come to light. Because of his age and poor play during last season with the Vancouver Canucks, Milstein’s announcement strongly suggests that Kane won’t return to the NHL. Although there were plenty of ups and downs, few players get to enjoy a 16-year career like Kane did. That career began on June 26, 2009, when the Atlanta Thrashers selected Kane with the fourth overall pick in the 2009 NHL Draft. He immediately jumped to the NHL, scoring 14 goals and 26 points in 66 games, good for a ninth-place finish in Calder Trophy voting. Kane spent one more season with the Thrashers and remained with the team when they relocated, becoming the second iteration of the Winnipeg Jets. His first season in Winnipeg is arguably his career-best campaign. The Vancouver, BC, native finished second on the team in scoring behind Blake Wheeler , registering 30 goals and 57 points in 74 games with a +11 rating. A few weeks before the 2012-13 campaign was supposed to start, the Jets signed Kane to a six-year, $31.5MM ($5.25MM AAV) extension. items.summary: Playing for the second time in 24 hours, the Flyers held the Canucks to just six shots through 40 minutes. “Yeah, there’s actually no excuse for that. It’s unacceptable to show up like this.”
items.body: VANCOUVER – It seems especially cruel — but typical — that what sure looks like the worst season in Vancouver Canucks ’ history will be extended by two games by the National Hockey League and its players’ association. On the other hand, an 84-game season, divided by four, means the Canucks have one more game to avoid manufacturing the NHL’s worst opening quarter since the salary-cap era began in 2005. So, despite an array of gruesome numbers surrounding the Canucks, arithmetic may still be their friend. They could use one. In Game 20 of the Canucks’ rebuild season, the Philadelphia Flyers, the third-worst team in the league and losers the night before in Calgary, not only dusted Vancouver 3-1 on Monday at Rogers Arena but held the home team to six shots through 40 minutes A third-period surge, which is to say the sudden reappearance of competitiveness, generated 13 shots for Vancouver and a power-play goal by Jonathan Lekkerimaki that brought the Canucks within one until Travis Sandheim’s empty-netter with 59 seconds remaining. The loss was the Canucks’ 16 th in 17 games and left them at 3-16-1 for the season. Twenty games was commonly regarded as the first quarter of an 82-game NHL schedule before the league extended each team’s docket to 84 games this season. items.body: SAN JOSE, Calif. — Ivar Stenberg scored the only goal in a shootout that lasted eight rounds, and the San Jose Sharks beat the New York Islanders 3-2 on Monday night to snap a five-game losing streak. Tyler Toffoli had a goal and an assist, and Stenberg also scored in regulation for the Sharks (8-11-1). Stenberg has six goals and is tied for the scoring lead among NHL rookies. Ben Hutton and Victor Eklund scored for the Islanders (7-6-4), who have lost four straight games (0-2-2). Ilya Sorokin stopped 37 shots. Stenberg put the Sharks on the board late in the first period after Toffoli sent a shot toward the net. Stenberg got a piece of the puck to redirect it past Sorokin and tie the game at 1. San Jose again rallied from a goal down midway through the second when Toffoli’s shot deflected off Islanders defenseman Adam Pelech and into the net. It was Toffoli’s first goal in eight games. Hutton opened the scoring early in the first after Simon Holmstrom’s pass found him with an open look. Eklund put New York ahead 2-1 early in the second with a power-play goal. Sharks center Alexander Wennberg, who returned after missing 10 games, was called for the penalty that led to the power play. The game got chippy late in the second as fights broke out, leading to four five-minute major penalties. Barclay Goodrow received a penalty for fighting Mitchell Chaffee, and Ty Dellandrea was penalized for fighting Kyle MacLean.

Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. items.title: McDavid’s historic assist streak ends in Oilers’ win over Rangers
items.body: For a second on Monday, it appeared that Connor McDavid had extended his historic assist streak to 19 games right at the buzzer in the Edmonton Oilers ' 3-1 win over the New York Rangers. But after a quick ruling from the NHL, McDavid had his helper on Leon Draisaitl's empty-net goal pulled off the scoresheet. As the Rangers pressed on the power play with their net empty in the final two minutes, a rebound came out to McDavid in front of the Oilers' net. Edmonton's captain bumped into New York forward JT Miller in the battle for the puck, which was eventually tipped out to Draisaitl closer to the blue line, where No. 29 flipped it down the ice and into the open cage. Upon closer inspection, Miller's stick was the last to touch the puck before Draisaitl put the game away — bringing McDavid's streak to an end at 18. With assists in 18 straight games, McDavid tied Adam Oates for the second-longest streak in NHL history, behind only Wayne Gretzky’s 23 games set in 1990-91. He did continue his point streak to open the season, however, opening the scoring with his 11th goal in Edmonton's first 19 games — giving him 48 points on the year.

items.body: Register Login Capitals Recall Justin Holl By Brennan McClain | at November 9, 2026 5:00 pm The Washington Capitals had a roster spot to fill after losing netminder Rémi Poirier off waivers earlier this afternoon. Washington quickly filled it, announcing they recalled defenseman Justin Holl from the AHL’s Hershey Bears. Holl, 34, earns his second call-up of the 2026-27 season. The Capitals signed Holl to a one-year, $900K contract this past offseason and recalled him earlier this season after Washington’s defensive corps suffered a few injuries. He looked good in his debut with Washington, scoring two goals in three games with a +1 rating, while averaging 12:59 of ice time per game. It’s a solid change of pace for Holl after the 10-year blueliner suffered through the worst stretch of his professional career with the Detroit Red Wings. Ahead of the 2023-24 season, the Red Wings signed Holl to a three-year, $10.2MM ($3.4MM AAV) contract after he spent the previous six years with the Toronto Maple Leafs. It started poorly, as Holl finished with only five assists in 38 games in his first season. Holl struggled again during the 2024-25 season, prompting Detroit to demote him. Last campaign, the final season of his three-year pact, Holl played exclusively for the Grand Rapids Griffins in the AHL before he was traded to the St. Louis Blues as a salary offset for the Justin Faulk trade. In fairness to Holl, he was never known as an offensive threat, but his production in Detroit was far lower than he was accustomed to in Toronto. Still, he also began to struggle defensively, producing a career-worst takeaway-to-turnover ratio in the 2024-25 season. Regardless, he has appeared far more comfortable in his limited action with the Capitals.

items.title: 'He Just Gave Up On Us': Jets' Arniel Talks Hellebuyck Trade, Devils' Decision To Sit Goalie Out
items.summary: Winnipeg Jets head coach Scott Arniel did not shy away when asked to share his thoughts on the New Jersey Devils' decision to sit Connor Hellebuyck ahead of his return to Canada Life Centre.
items.body: James Carey Lauder-Imagn Images James Carey Lauder-Imagn Images 'He Just Gave Up On Us': Jets' Arniel Talks Hellebuyck Trade, Devils' Decision To Sit Goalie Out Eric Cruikshank Partner Nov 9, 2026 8:51 PM Published Nov 9, 2026 8:51 PM Updated Nov 9, 2026 10:03 PM Winnipeg Jets head coach Scott Arniel did not shy away when asked to share his thoughts on the New Jersey Devils' decision to sit Connor Hellebuyck ahead of his return to Canada Life Centre. The Winnipeg Jets and their fans were hoping for some closure this week. After a lengthy standoff between the franchise and three-time Vezina Trophy winner Connor Hellebuyck resulted in the 33-year-old being traded to the New Jersey Devils , this week had the potential for the netminder to face his former teammates and the fanbase he played in front of for the previous 11 seasons. However, after Devils GM Sunny Mehta announced on Sunday evening that Hellebuyck would not be starting in net for the team's Nov. 10 matchup against the Jets at Canada Life Centre, Winnipeg head coach Scott Arniel was among many critics around the hockey world who were disappointed by the decision. More Videos "We've seen some other players go back to their buildings and do it and get it over and done with," Arniel said to media in Winnipeg on Monday. "I know it's their decision and they can do whatever they want, but I think that it would put closure (to the situation). This doesn't. "We're gonna see them in (nine) games in their building and I'm sure he's going to be in the net then." The Jets will be capping off a three-game Eastern Conference road trip on Nov. 28 with a rematch in New Jersey. The Devils do not return to Winnipeg for the rest of the season.
